nodes.question: What might businesses look for in a biodiversity indicator?
nodes.answer: Businesses might look for an easy-to-track, target-oriented indicator.
nodes.paragraph: In these contexts, indicators are used to assess (bio-diversity) impacts linked to different LU change drivers, whichincludes accountability for historical impacts or identi cation of cur- rent pressures 4 6. nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What categories do scientists use to classify bird populations in urban settings?
nodes.answer: Scientists classify bird populations in urban settings into categories based on their population dynamics: dwellers, utilizers, and avoiders.
nodes.paragraph: 2008 ; Escobar- lb ez and MacGregor-Fors 2016 ; Marzluff 2016 ; Sun et al. 2022 ). Birds inhabiting urban areas are exposed to a large variety of physiological stress sources, such as predation by opportunistic scavengers (e.g., cats, dogs, raccoons, crows), parasitic diseases, and collisions with anthropogenic struc - tures (e.g., vehicles, bus shelters, windows; Klem 1989 ; Marzluff 2001 ; Loss et al. 2015 ; Santiago-Alarcon and Delgado-V 2017 ; Zy k-Gorczy ska et al. 2020 ). Despite all the above, bird species have different responses to environ - mental changes, some of them even adapting and thriving in these transformed habitats over time (Croci et al. 2008 ; McDonnell and Hahs 2015 ; Patankar et al. 2021 ). These differential responses have allowed scientists to classify them into different categories according to their population dynamics within cities (i.e., dwellers, utilizers, avoiders; see Fischer et al. 2015 ).
